subject: Linguistics
title: Literal Versus Figurative Meaning
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Literal Versus Figurative Meaning.

hook.text: When someone says 'break a leg,' they definitely do not want you injured.

buildup.text: Figurative language stretches words beyond their dictionary definitions.

discovery.text: Metaphor, irony, and idioms all rely on listeners understanding the non-literal intent.

twist.text: Children and language learners take idioms literally at first—comedy ensues.

climax.text: About six percent of everyday English sentences contain at least one metaphor.

punchline.text: Half of what we say isn't what we mean.

quiz.question: What type of language is 'break a leg'?
